newsitem.title: UK: Flemings bullish on emerging mkts, Latam top pick.
newsitem.headline: Flemings bullish on emerging mkts, Latam top pick.

text.p: Robert Fleming & Co said on Monday it expected dollar returns of about 20 percent in emerging equity markets in 1997, with Latin America likely to offer the best regional return in the near term.
"The bull case for emerging markets is highly potent," it said in a monthly report. "We see dollar returns approaching 20 percent over 12 months, without assuming PER (price/earnings) expansion."

Its global emerging markets research team said the temptation to put money made in booming developed markets into emerging markets had proved difficult to resist this year, and the asset diversification should continue on anything other than a crash scenario.
Within emerging markets, local investors were also switching into equities from bonds and deposits.

It was overweight Latin America which had been the focus of global investor liquidity, and despite the region being hurt by worries about a U.S. tightening, sentiment should recover quickly. Brazil was its top Latam pick.

Flemings said liquidity should shift to Asia later in the year although there were no signs yet of this happening. Its neutral position on Asia masked differing stances on individual markets, with Hong Kong, Malaysia and the Philippines positive and Thailand and Korea underperforming.
It said it was underweight Europe, Middle East and Africa as it did not wish to have too great an exposure to South Africa on a global basis, but it was positive on smaller markets in the region.
"We favour the smaller markets in Africa which now offer good absolute and relative value."
The report said it was overweight on Egypt and Russia for the medium term on asset values, while the Czech and Turkish markets should be underweighted on macroeconomic concerns.
